quick.summary: Add an index so your database can jump straight to a row without reading everything.
quick.takeaway: Searching without an index forces the database to read every single row.

beats.line: My search took ten minutes on a huge table. Why so slow?
Imagine finding one specific recipe in a giant cookbook.
I would use the index at the back of the book.
Right. Without it, you have to read every single page.
Your database is reading every row to find one match.
This is known as a full table scan.
Can I just say reading the whole book?
That works perfectly. Reading the whole book takes forever.
Add an index to the column you search most often.
So the index helps it jump straight to the right row.
Exactly. Now your search takes ten milliseconds.

quiz.question: What happens when you run a search on a large table that has no index?
options: The database reads every single row sequentially to find a match.
The query gets blocked and automatically deletes your saved records.
The database automatically creates a temporary index in the background.
The search completes instantly but returns random chunks of data.
quiz.explanation: Without an index, the database has no shortcut. It must check every row one by one, which is incredibly slow.

quiz.question: An index acts like a map, helping the database jump directly to the right piece of data.
quiz.explanation: Just like a book index points you straight to a page, a database index points the query directly to the correct row.
